newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norsk Hydro in Asian investment venture.
newsitem.headline: Norsk Hydro in Asian investment venture.

text.p: Norwegian industrial group Norsk Hydro ASA said on Tuesday it had signed an agreement to establish a joint venture company with Temasek Holdings (Private) Ltd, the investment arm of the Singapore government, to invest in industrial projects in Asia.
The venture, Hydro Asia Pacific Pte Ltd is 65 percent owned by Norsk Hydro and 35 percent by Temasek.

"This joint venture represents a long-term cooperation between Norsk Hydro and Temasek to invest more effectively in industrial projects and businesses in Asia," Egil Myklebust, President of Norsk Hydro, said in a statement.

Hydro Asia Pacific will invest in Norsk Hydro's core businesses, namely fertilisers, petrochemicals, industrial gases and aluminium metal products, with a geographical focus in ASEAN, Greater China and India.
"To supply these markets with energy-intensive dproducts, investments could also be made in countries outside of Asia," Hydro's statement said.

Quek Poh Huat, Temasek President, said: "This is an excellent opportunity for Temasek to enter into a strategic partnership with one of Europe's leading industrial groups with proven technology and industrial expertise."
In October Temasek entered a memorandum of understanding with the Daimler-Benz Group for joint venture investments in Asia.
